title: Design Insights from the Landscape of Sustainability Apps: A Guide for Developers
content: This paper explores the role of mobile applications in promoting sustainable behaviors and environmental awareness. Recognizing the importance of digital technologies in environmental advocacy, the study examines how design strategies in sustainability-focused apps influence user engagement, ethical perceptions, and motivation. Using a mixed-methods exploratory approach, the researcher analyzed 54 mobile applications from the Google Play Store, categorized by interaction type (informative, gamified, or both), environmental theme (e.g., ethical consumption, carbon tracking), and user review availability. Of these, 21 apps with user feedback were further analyzed using Natural Language Processing techniques. Sentiment analysis with the VADER model assessed overall user satisfaction, while Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) identified common themes and concerns in user reviews. The findings highlight that app success relies not just on informative content or basic gamification, but on clear, motivational content that links sustainability goals to practical daily actions. Users value straightforward interfaces, consistent performance, and ethical accessibility. Crucially, the study identifies three often-overlooked but essential elements in mainstream app design: inclusivity, affordability, and transparency. The thesis emphasizes that these factors significantly impact user trust and long-term engagement. Based on user feedback, the research offers practical design recommendations for developers to create ethical, user-centered, and context-sensitive sustainability apps. Overall, the thesis contributes to the field of digital sustainability by bridging design principles with user expectations, aiming to enhance the impact of mobile technology in fostering sustainable lifestyles
